newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks close firm on blue chip trading.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks close firm on blue chip trading.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed steady in active Friday trading which was focused on blue chips, brokers said. Foreign investors were main participant.
The all share index closed 0.44 points higher at 578.14, but off 579.81 at mid-morning break.
"Deals got done because buyers have moved up a little to meet sellers," said Alistair Corera of brokerage Forbes & Walker. Some investors took profits later.
Trading was dominated foreigners, who bought 73.49 million rupees worth of shares and sold 81.15 million worth, against the day's turnover of 94.14 million
Local institutional and retail investors joined the fray, picking up selected blue chips, brokers said.
Price gains were led by holding company Aitken Spence which rose five rupees to 130 and Ceylon Tobacco which rose one rupee to 29.50.
Among active shares were Aitken Spence, Blue Diamonds, Ceylon Tobacco, Development Finance, Dockyard, John Keells Holdings and Richard Pieris.
